finding.text: `audit_session` must not be in the rewrite list in `Servex/ext/remote/RemoteMCP.js` `intercept()` (the `/^(session_summary|session_line|quick_fix|audit_session)$/` line). Its `session` argument is a Claude session uuid, and those are never in `servex.sessions.map`, so every call from the voice app gets its uuid swapped for the `v-` voice id and audits nothing. Keep the rewrite for the tools that take a `v-` id: `session_summary`, `session_line` and `quick_fix`.

The brief asked for "the day's voice session", but `voice_session()` makes a new session for each MCP connection (keyed by `mcp-session-id`). Every time the Claude app reconnects, the day gets another `v-…` folder. That may be the better choice, but `doc/voice-logging.md` should say it was chosen on purpose.

The test's fake `sessions.create` (`RemoteMCP.test.mjs`, the `servex` stub) writes no line 1, so the test only checks the fallback header written by `RemoteMCP.js`. The real `Sessions.create` writes its own line 1 without `caller`, so `lines[0].session.caller === "voice-app"` passes here but would not be true in production. Also, `row.caller` is set after `store.save()`, so it is not saved until something else saves.
`Sessions.create({ path: "/live/" })` calls `point()`, which posts a "started" line on `/live/` for every new connection. Check whether that is wanted on the owner's presentation screen.
In `record()` in `RemoteMCP.js`, the `catch {}` hides a failed write, so a lost owner line would leave no trace. Log it with `console.error`, as `voice_session()` already does.

Plan steps 4 and 5 have no evidence in the diff. Step 4: does `/live/sessions/` list the folder? Step 5: the smoke test on a private port, and a `Note:` card about the Servex restart. The doc says the work is "live after a Servex restart".

`register_session` still advertises `required: ["id", "session_id"]` (Servex/agents/External.js:156, and `RemoteMCP.tools()` passes `required` through unchanged), but the new INSTRUCTIONS line in Servex/ext/remote/RemoteMCP.js:19 says "no arguments needed". A client that checks the schema, or a model that follows it, sends an `id`. Then `!target.id` in `intercept()` is false, the call goes to `External.register`, and it registers an external agent instead of returning the `v-` voice session. Fix: drop `required` for this tool in `tools()`, or have `intercept()` answer every `register_session` call that has no live `session_id`.

The `spawned` line will almost always have `task_dir: null` in real use. `after()` (Servex/ext/remote/RemoteMCP.js, the new `after` method) reads `j.task_dir ?? j.task?.dir ?? j.dir` from the spawn_agent result, but the real result is `agent.card()` (Servex/agents/Agents.js:1430), which holds no task dir at all. The test hides this because its stub `spawn_agent` (RemoteMCP.test.mjs, the new `mcp.tool({ name: "spawn_agent" … })` line) returns a made-up `task_dir`. Fix: pass the call's args into `after()` and read the dir from `args.task?.dir` (the spawn-by-brief shape), and make the stub return a real `card()` shape.

The cloud row has `home: "/live/"`, so `Sessions.recent({page:"/live/"})` (Servex/agents/Sessions.js:737) will list it. Within the one-hour resume window, a browser drawer opened on /live/ could resume into `cloud-voice-agent-YYYYMMDD` (Sessions.js:702) and wake fast/smart agents for it. Either give it a home of its own, the day folder, or skip `kind: "cloud-voice-agent"` rows in `create()`'s resume.

The handmade row breaks the store's conventions. Its `at` is a UTC ISO string where `Sessions` uses `now_ms()` (Sessions.js:105). It also has no `path`, `project` or `host`, and the chat lines at Sessions.js:325/449 read `s.path`. Minting it through a small `Sessions` method (for example `Sessions.daily(kind, caller)`) would keep the row shape in one place, which is Law 6, instead of RemoteMCP building a store row by hand.

The day is computed from local time (`getDate()`), but the line-1 `at` is UTC (`toISOString()`). After 7 pm Central, the header's date and the folder's date differ. Use `now_ms()` or `TaskDirs.day()`, which RemoteMCP already imports (RemoteMCP.js:103).

`record()` now creates `this.sessions[sid]` on the fly but never calls `save_sessions()`. That is harmless, since `last_words` only de-duplicates, but it is a silent side store. `voice_session(sid)` at RemoteMCP.js:147 still passes an argument the new signature ignores.
